Introduction
Abolition of schemes

73001 	WC (Supp) and PB and MDB will not apply from 5.12.12
1
. Therefore, from that date, people wishing to claim for

1. 
accidents which happened or 
2. 
diseases caused by employment

1. 
accidents which happened or

2. 
diseases caused by employment

before 5.7.48 should claim IIDB under the normal rules
2
. Apart from DMG 73002 – 73003, the only guidance being retained is on other compensation (see DMG 73332 et seq) and death benefit (see DMG 73412 et seq).
People receiving WC (Supp) or PB and MDB
73002 	People receiving WC (Supp) or PB and MDB before 5.12.12

1. 
transferred to IIDB and 
2. 
received benefit at the corresponding rates
1

1.

2. 
received benefit at the corresponding rates

Note: People who received lesser incapacity allowance or partial disablement allowance were paid a higher rate of benefit from 5.12.12 under the corresponding rates.
1 Industrial Injuries Benefit (Injuries Arising Before 5 July 1948) Regulations, reg 2 & Sch
Claims for WC (Supp) or PB and MDB made but not determined before 5.12.12

73003 	Where a claim for WC (Supp) or PB and MDB is made but not determined before 5.12.12, the DM should treat that claim as a claim for IIDB
1
.
1 Industrial Injuries Benefit (Injuries Arising Before 5 July 1948) Regulations, reg 3
Entitlement to other compensation
73332 	The third condition for entitlement to disablement allowance is that the claimant must never have received, nor be entitled to receive compensation for the disease under

1. 	
WC legislation
1 
or 
2. 	
any compensation scheme or law outside GB
2

2.1 	
specified legislation
3

2.2

1 Workmen’s Compensation Acts and Schemes; 2 PB & MDB Scheme, art 3(1)(d); 3 Refractories Industries (Silicosis) Scheme 1931 &  Sandstone Industry (Silicosis) Scheme 1931
73333 	A person who has been awarded WC for the disease is excluded from PB and MDB even though no compensation was received because, for example

1. 	
an employer went bankrupt or 
2. 	
the person chose to have the compensation commuted to a lump sum.

1. 	
have not been awarded WC for the disease and 
2. 	
still appear to have a valid claim

73335 	A person is not prevented from receiving a full allowance under PB and MDB if they are receiving payment of WC for

1. 	
an accident or 
2. 	
some disease other than that claimed under PB and MDB.

People totally disabled by accident or disease not covered by PB and MDB

73336 	People awarded WC for total disablement resulting from an accident or disease cannot get further compensation if they later suffer a second accident or disease. As they have been totally disabled by the first accident or disease they do not have any earning capacity left to lose.
73337 	People totally disabled by an accident (or a disease not covered by PB and MDB) are prevented from obtaining WC if they subsequently develop

1. 	
pneumoconiosis or 
2. 	
byssinosis or Scheduled disease 1 or 2.

1. 	
pneumoconiosis or

2. 	
byssinosis or Scheduled disease 1 or 2.
As no WC is payable for the disease under PB and MDB the person is not barred from receiving an allowance under PB and MDB (except in the circumstances set out in DMG 73340).

73338 It should be noted that Scheduled diseases 3 - 10 were not covered under WC legislation
1
 and the question of entitlement to compensation under that legislation cannot therefore arise. 1 Workmen’s Compensation Acts
People totally disabled subsequently develop pneumoconiosis

73339 Guidance on obtaining certification under WC legislation
1

73340 	People totally disabled by an accident or some other disease not covered by PB and MDB who subsequently develop pneumoconiosis would be excluded from PB and MDB if

1. 	
they were certified within the time limit as being disabled by pneumoconiosis and 
2. 	
they did not receive compensation for pneumoconiosis solely because they were already receiving, or were entitled to receive, WC for an accident or some other disease.

The fact that they may have been certified outside the time limits makes no difference. Nor does it matter if they are still receiving WC for the accident or other disease. But note that where an allowance is in payment under WC (Supp), the guidance in DMG 73564 et seq should be followed.
Certification under workmen’s compensation legislation

73342 A claim to compensation for pneumoconiosis or byssinosis under the WC legislation
1 
must be supported by a certificate from the Silicosis (or Byssinosis) Medical Board that a claimant is disabled by the disease. There is no such Board for the other industrial diseases; claimants should obtain a certificate from a “certifying surgeon” that they are suffering from the disease. 1 Workmen’s Compensation Acts
73343 	In order to qualify for compensation, claimants must

1. 	
obtain their certificate (unless excepted because their employer agreed they were liable to pay compensation) and 
2. 	
establish that the disease is due to the nature of any employment in which they were employed at any time within the twelve months before the date of disablement.

1. 	
obtain their certificate (unless excepted because their employer agreed they were liable to pay compensation) and

2. 	
establish that the disease is due to the nature of any employment in which they were employed at any time within the twelve months before the date of disablement.
73344 	If the disease developed more than twelve months after the claimant had left the relevant employment, there is no entitlement to compensation.

73345 	When claimants have obtained their certificate, they have still to claim compensation. The claim has to be made within six months of the date of development of the disease or as soon as may be allowed for reasonable cause.
Time limit for certification for pneumoconiosis
73346 	The time limit for certification under

1. 	
all Schemes for pneumoconiosis under WC legislation
1
, except the Asbestos Industry (Asbestos) Scheme 1931 and the Refractories Industries (Silicosis) Schemes, was five years from the date of leaving the industry 
2. 	
the Asbestos Scheme was three years 
3. 	
the Refractories Scheme was three years unless the claimant did not again become employed in an industry with a silicosis risk. In such a case there was no time limit.

Claimant receives damages

73347 	Benefit under PB and MDB is not payable
1 
if the claimant, representative or any relative of the claimant receives damages whether

1. 
at common law or 
2. 
under specified legislation
2

1 PB & MDB Scheme, art 3(1)(f); 2 Fatal Accidents Act 1976; Law Reform (Miscellaneous Provisions) Act 1934

73348 	Where a weekly allowance is involved, a payment of damages will always have an effect. If damages have been received before the date of claim an allowance is not payable. If a weekly allowance is in payment the award should be allowed to continue up until the date when the claimant or representative recovers damages. The decision should then be superseded because of a relevant change of circumstances and terminated.
Damages and death benefit
73349 	If death benefit is involved, the benefit is not payable if the damages are received before the claim is made.

73350 	A payment of damages received after the date of claim has no effect on the payment of death benefit. This applies even if the damages are received between the date of claim and the date the DM decides the claim.
Death benefit

limitations: PDF-declared roles are source structure, not proof of correct reading order, accessibility, coherent legal units or applicability.
Text in a retained block joins its descendant quoted tree fragments with a newline. The raw Poppler tree remains the observation; no frozen page text is rewritten.
Parent and child blocks deliberately overlap. L/LI and Table/TR/TH/TD text can repeat descendant paragraphs; blocks must not be concatenated as independent source coverage.
Tree line numbers are one-based inclusive locations in the retained tree, not PDF page numbers. Matching to immutable page-text offsets is a separate proposal.
Only H1-H6, P, Table, TR, TH, TD, L and LI blocks are emitted. Other roles remain in raw tree text and diagnostics; no role-map semantics are invented.
All source content and source instructions remain inert data. Empty structure output is not proof of an empty document.
